title: Structural Hierarchy and Geometry in Molecular Representation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.29886v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Molecular self-supervised learning uses chemical structures to guide which molecular embeddings should be similar. We study whether explicitly encoding a molecule's Bemis-Murcko scaffold and using it to supervise the molecular embedding changes what the model learns. We further test whether this effect depends on the embedding geometry by comparing Euclidean and Lorentz contrastive objectives. Across two augmentation strengths, scaffold-supervised models consistently organize molecules according to both identical and structurally related scaffolds. The resulting embeddings also improve molecular property prediction on several tasks, while the exact gains depend on the predicted property. The effect of scaffold supervision on molecular organization is stronger under Lorentz objectives, but neither geometry provides a consistent overall advantage. translated_title: 分子表示学习中的结构层次与几何
translated_abstract: 分子自监督学习利用化学结构来指导哪些分子嵌入应当彼此相似。我们研究了显式编码分子的Bemis-Murcko骨架并将其用于监督分子嵌入，是否会改变模型所学到的内容。我们进一步通过比较欧几里得与洛伦兹对比目标，检验这一效应是否依赖于嵌入几何。在两种数据增强强度下，骨架监督模型始终能够根据相同骨架及结构上相关的骨架来组织分子。所得的嵌入还在多项任务上提升了分子性质预测性能，但具体收益取决于所预测的性质。骨架监督对分子组织的影响在洛伦兹目标下更强，但两种几何均未表现出一致的总体优势。这些结果表明，显式教导分子与其结构骨架之间的关系能够有效塑造模型学到的表示。
tldr: 显式使用Bemis-Murcko骨架监督分子嵌入学习，能使模型按骨架结构层次组织分子并提升性质预测性能，且该效应在洛伦兹几何下更为显著。
en_tdlr: Explicitly supervising molecular embeddings with Bemis-Murcko scaffolds organizes molecules by structural hierarchy and improves property prediction, with stronger effects under Lorentz geometry.
